page: Google Cloud Platform h4d-standard-192 is a compute-optimized instance powered by dedicated AMD EPYC 9B45 processors based on the x86_64 architecture. The machine configuration provides 192 dedicated physical cores and 192 vCPUs with one thread per core, paired with 720 GB of system memory, yielding 3.75 GB of RAM per core. The processor topology includes 48 KB of L1 data cache, 1 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache, alongside hardware support for vector and cryptographic instruction sets including AVX-512 (VNNI, BF16) and VAES. The configuration contains no attached GPUs and provides no bundled local storage.

In synthetic and computational benchmarks, the h4d-standard-192 demonstrates top-tier multi-threaded throughput. It achieved a multi-core stress-ng score of 655,072.06 and a single-core score of 3,461.39. Memory subsystems show top-tier bandwidth, delivering 1,054.65 GB/sec in uncached 256 MB block reads and 427.73 GB/sec in block writes. Extended instruction tests in PassMark scored 441,026.50 alongside an encryption score of 274,650.81, reflecting strong vector execution capabilities. Data processing benchmarks demonstrated 495.56 million operations per second on Redis SET operations and a multi-threaded bzip3 decompression throughput of 2,808.49 GB/sec.

The high compute density and dedicated one-to-one core mapping eliminate hyper-threading contention, making this server profile technically efficient for highly parallelized batch execution. However, the total absence of integrated local storage requires reliance on network storage volumes, which should be accounted for in I/O-intensive architectures. With 720 GB of system memory, the instance is appropriate for CPU-bound simulations, large-scale software compilation pipelines, parallel scientific computations, and in-memory batch processing.
description: Google Cloud Platform h4d-standard-192 is a high-density, compute-optimized virtual machine powered by 192 dedicated physical cores of AMD EPYC 9B45 processors on the x86_64 architecture. Featuring a single thread per core and 720 GB of total RAM, it allocates approximately 3.75 GB of memory per core. The AMD CPU features AVX-512 vector support (including BF16 and VNNI) alongside hardware encryption acceleration via VAES and AES. In standardized performance evaluations, the instance ranks in the top tier for multi-core throughput, posting a stress-ng multi-core score of 655,072.06 and an uncached memory read bandwidth of 1,054.65 GB/sec. It includes zero GPUs and no local storage, requiring network-attached storage for disk operations. This hardware configuration is suited for compute-intensive workloads that demand raw parallel processing and dedicated execution cores without thread contention, such as scientific simulations, high-throughput distributed compilation, in-memory data transformations, and heavy cryptographic processing.
